ui.bannerTitle: Veterinary Dermatology & Canine Bathing Interval Algorithm
ui.bannerP1: Unlike human epidermis (which has 10–15 cell layers and an acidic pH of 5.5), canine skin is extraordinarily delicate:
ui.bannerStrong: 3 to 5 cell layers thick with a neutral pH of 7.0 to 7.4
ui.bannerP2: Over-bathing with harsh detergents strips the protective lipid barrier and kills beneficial commensal skin flora, causing rebound seborrhea and chronic pruritus. This calculator balances coat architecture, environmental exposure, and dermatological skin conditions to prescribe the optimal bathing frequency.
ui.section1Desc: Different follicle patterns dictate natural oil distribution and debris retention
ui.coatShortSmoothDesc: Low-maintenance single layer. Natural sebum protects skin; frequent washing causes flaking.
ui.coatShortSmoothExamples: Boxer, Beagle, Dalmatian, Doberman, French Bulldog, Weimaraner
ui.coatShortSmoothDrying: Towel dry followed by ambient air drying or low-speed room temperature blow.
ui.coatDoubleDesc: Dense insulating undercoat + water-repellent guard hairs. Frequent shampooing strips thermal insulation.
ui.coatDoubleExamples: Golden Retriever, German Shepherd, Husky, Pomeranian, Bernese Mountain Dog
ui.coatDoubleDrying: High-velocity cool dryer essential to separate undercoat down to the skin and prevent acute moist dermatitis (hot spots).
ui.coatCurlyDesc: Continuous hair growth that traps debris, dander, and environmental allergens readily.
ui.coatCurlyExamples: Poodle, Goldendoodle, Labradoodle, Bichon Frise, Schnauzer, Airedale
ui.coatCurlyDrying: High-velocity blow dry with slicker brush fluffing to detangle damp curls before mats tighten.
ui.coatLongSilkyDesc: Fine hair prone to tangling, static, and picking up burrs and road grit.
ui.coatLongSilkyExamples: Yorkshire Terrier, Shih Tzu, Maltese, Afghan Hound, Cocker Spaniel
ui.coatLongSilkyDrying: Gentle towel press (no circular rubbing to avoid tangles); blow dry on low heat with pin brush.
ui.coatHairlessDesc: No fur barrier to absorb natural skin sebum and environmental soot; prone to clogged blackhead pores.
ui.coatHairlessExamples: Chinese Crested, Xoloitzcuintli, American Hairless Terrier
ui.coatHairlessDrying: Soft pat dry followed immediately by dog-safe non-comedogenic ceramide skin moisturizer.
ui.section2Desc: Accounts for dirt, organic manure, and surface mud accumulation
ui.lifestyleIndoorDesc: Paved leash walks only. Minimal mud, grass pollen, or wet soil exposure.
ui.lifestyleModerateDesc: Daily backyard play, casual dog park visits, standard weather exposure.
ui.lifestyleOutdoorDesc: Swimming in lakes/oceans, digging in topsoil, hiking dense forested terrain.
ui.lifestyleFarmDesc: Constant livestock manure, heavy mud, burrs, and intense daily farm labor.
ui.section3Desc: Clinical skin conditions alter bathing frequency from hygiene to therapy
ui.skinHealthyShampoo: Soap-free hypoallergenic oatmeal or gentle aloe conditioning canine shampoo (pH 6.5–7.5).
ui.skinHealthyCaution: Avoid human shampoos: human skin is acidic (pH 5.5) whereas canine skin is neutral (pH 7.0–7.4). Human soap degrades the stratum corneum barrier.
ui.skinDryFlakyShampoo: Lipid-restoring colloidal oatmeal with phytosphingosine and essential fatty acids.
ui.skinDryFlakyCaution: Space baths further apart. Rinse thoroughly with cool-to-lukewarm water; hot water strips epidermal lipids.
ui.skinAtopicShampoo: Medicated ceramide shampoo or chlorhexidine rinse to physically wash away trapped environmental allergens.
ui.skinAtopicCaution: Bathing acts as mechanical decontamination: washing pollen off paws and belly weekly reduces systemic pruritus (itching).
ui.skinYeastShampoo: Veterinary prescription 2%–4% Chlorhexidine + Ketoconazole / Miconazole medicated shampoo.
ui.skinYeastCaution: Must leave shampoo lather on skin for a full 10-minute contact time before rinsing to allow antimicrobial penetration.
ui.brushEvery: Brush coat every {{days}} days between baths
ui.swimAdviceBody1: After lake, river, or saltwater swims,
ui.swimAdviceBody2: rinse thoroughly with plain tap water
ui.swimAdviceBody3: without shampoo. This removes corrosive salt crystals and chlorine without depleting natural skin oils.
ui.doubleCoatBody: Shaving Golden Retrievers, Huskies, or Shepherds destroys the thermal air insulation layer, permanently damages coat regrowth (post-clipping alopecia), and increases heatstroke risk.

none.title: Full Flighted (Veterinary Recommended)
lines: Cardiovascular Health: Flying uses 10–20× more energy than walking, preventing fatal avian atherosclerosis and fatty liver.
Psychological Confidence: Flighted birds exhibit significantly lower rates of chronic scream-calling, phobias, and feather self-mutilation.
Home Safety Mandate: All ceiling fans MUST be turned OFF, windows covered with decals or blinds, open cookware covered, and doors closed.

conservative.title: Conservative Micro-Clip (Glide Preserved)
lines: Trim only the outer 4 to 6 primary flight feathers on BOTH wings symmetrically.
Allows the bird to glide safely to the floor at a 45° angle; prevents upward lift while eliminating crash landing fractures.
NEVER trim secondary flight feathers (inner wing) or covert protective feathers.

aggressive.title: Severe / Single-Wing Clip (Strictly Prohibited)
lines: Severe Danger: Cutting too short causes the bird to drop like a rock, shattering the keel bone (sternum) and splitting the skin.
Single-Wing Asymmetry: Clipping one wing causes catastrophic corkscrew spins into walls and floors.
Blood Feather Lethality: Trimming dark, active growing blood feathers causes profuse hemorrhaging.

canine-fluid-therapy-calculator.description: Clinical fluid therapy calculator for dogs recovering from surgery or illness. Calculates dehydration deficit, daily maintenance, ongoing losses, pump hourly infusion rate, and gravity drip speeds.

ui.bannerBody: This fluid therapy calculator adheres to the **AAHA (American Animal Hospital Association)** and **WSAVA** fluid therapy guidelines for canine post-operative recovery, shock resuscitation, and dehydration restoration. Always monitor patient lung sounds, PCV/TP, and urine output to prevent fluid overload.
ui.tierMarkers0: Moist, pink gums; immediate skin turgor recoil (<1s); bright alert eyes; capillary refill time (CRT) < 2s.
ui.tierMarkers5: Slightly tacky mucous membranes; normal skin turgor; eyes normal; CRT ~2s.
ui.tierMarkers7: Dry/sticky gums; slight loss of skin turgor (delayed skin fold recoil 2–3s); CRT 2–3s; mild depression.
ui.tierMarkers10: Marked skin tenting (skin stays pinched >3s); dull sunken eyes (enophthalmos); dry pale gums; CRT > 3s; cold paws.
ui.tierMarkers12: Persistent skin tenting; deeply sunken eyes; signs of hypovolemic shock; weak rapid pulse; cold extremities; depressed consciousness.
ui.correctionHint: Deficit volume is distributed across this duration.
ui.lossesHint: Compensates for surgical fluids, drains, and gastrointestinal loss.
ui.dripOpt15: Standard Macro-drip Set (15 gtt/mL) — Common for medium/large dogs
ui.dripOpt10: Heavy Macro-drip Set (10 gtt/mL) — Large & Giant breeds
ui.dripOpt60: Pediatric Micro-drip Set (60 gtt/mL) — Small dogs & puppies (<10 kg)
ui.pumpRateHint: Continuous IV infusion rate during recovery
ui.urineAfter: (1.0 to 2.0 mL/kg/hr) to confirm renal recovery and prevent anuria.
ui.emptyState: Enter your dog's weight to calculate the fluid prescription.
ui.refTitle: Post-Operative Fluid Monitoring & Fluid Overload Warning Signs
ui.refCrystalloidsBody: Balanced electrolyte solutions such as **Lactated Ringer's Solution (LRS)**, **Normosol-R**, or **Plasmalyte-A** are preferred. Avoid pure 0.9% NaCl for prolonged maintenance unless hypochloremia or Addisonian crisis is present.
ui.refOverloadBody: Serous nasal discharge, chemosis (swelling of the conjunctiva), tachypnea (rapid breathing), moist lung crackles, restlessness, and sudden excessive body weight gain. Reduce rate immediately if noted.
ui.refHypothermiaBody: Use fluid warmers or warm IV lines when administering fluids post-surgery to prevent anesthesia-induced hypothermia, which delays drug clearance and prolongs recovery times.

budgie.name: Budgerigar
budgie.nutrition: Egg food (scrambled hard-boiled egg with crushed shell), sprouted seeds, high-methionine amino acids.
budgie.pinCare: Provide extra shallow baths to soften keratin sheaths; budgie head pin feathers can be gently rolled if bonded.

cockatiel.name: Cockatiel
cockatiel.nutrition: Boiled egg yolk, dark leafy greens (kale, dandelion), calcium cuttlebone, beta-carotene (carrots).
cockatiel.pinCare: Cockatiels cannot reach their own crest; bonded mates or gentle owner head preening helps open mature sheaths.

conure.name: Conure (Green Cheek / Sun)
conure.nutrition: Sprouted pulses, cooked quinoa, sweet potatoes, raw red palm oil (rich in Vitamin A & E).
conure.pinCare: Mist daily with warm water to relieve intense prickling sensations on neck and flanks.

african-grey.name: African Grey
african-grey.nutrition: Bioavailable calcium (crushed oyster shell, steamed collards), raw organic red palm fruit oil.
african-grey.pinCare: Extremely sensitive pin feathers; avoid touching blood feathers in active shaft growth.

amazon.name: Amazon Parrot
amazon.nutrition: Steam-cooked orange squash, dark leafy greens, high-potency organic pellets.
amazon.pinCare: Heavy warm showers accelerate sheath breakdown and reduce irritable moodiness.

cockatoo.name: Cockatoo
cockatoo.nutrition: Higher amino acid profile; avoid excess high-fat seeds, emphasize broccoli and leafy sprouts.
cockatoo.pinCare: Intense powder down increase; increase air filtration and daily baths.

macaw.name: Large Macaw
macaw.frequency: Shed in sequence (takes up to 3 months)
macaw.nutrition: Raw in-shell walnuts, Brazil nuts, palm fruit oil, complex extruded pellets.
macaw.pinCare: Massive primary flight feather shafts; do NOT pull tight sheath until dry and flaky.

budgie.name: Budgerigar (Australian Grassland)
budgie.hormonal: If female budgies start searching for dark nesting corners, extend sleep to 12 hours of total darkness to suppress breeding hormones.

canary.name: Canary / Finch

cockatiel.name: Cockatiel
cockatiel.hormonal: CRITICAL FOR FEMALE COCKATIELS: Chronic egg laying is triggered by long daylight (>14 hrs). Maintain 12–14 hours of total dark coverage to prevent fatal egg binding.

lovebird.name: Lovebird
lovebird.hormonal: Cover cage with breathable blackout fabric; prevent access to shredded paper or enclosed dark huts.

conure.name: Conure (Green Cheek / Sun)
conure.hormonal: Sleep deprivation triggers aggressive screaming and territorial cage aggression. Provide quiet sleep retreat.

african-grey.suggestion: 8:00 PM – 8:00 AM (12 hours in dedicated sleep cage)

amazon.name: Amazon Parrot
amazon.hormonal: Spring hormonal 'hot-headed' behavior is reduced by enforcing 12+ hours of strict uninterrupted darkness.

cockatoo.name: Cockatoo
cockatoo.hormonal: Inadequate sleep leads directly to severe neurotic screaming and self-mutilation (feather chewing/picking).

macaw.name: Large Macaw
macaw.hormonal: Equatorial jungle species naturally evolved with equal 12-hour day / 12-hour night cycles.

ui.phase1Text: Colors fade, belly turns light pink.
ui.phase2Text: Lymph fluid separates old skin. Snake is blind & defensive.
ui.phase3Text: Eyes turn clear 24–48h before active shed.

ball-python.name: Ball Python (Python regius)
ball-python.tips: Snakes must shed in ONE complete piece from nose to tail tip including both transparent eye caps (brilles). Never pull dry shed.

corn-snake.name: Corn Snake
corn-snake.tips: Provide a rough cork bark or stone surface for the snake to rub its snout against to start the skin roll.

leopard-gecko.name: Leopard Gecko
leopard-gecko.tips: Geckos eat their shed skin (keratophagy) to reclaim calcium and nutrients and hide their scent from predators. Check toes after every shed.

bearded-dragon.name: Bearded Dragon
bearded-dragon.tips: Lizards shed in large separate patches over days. Never pull shed before it separates freely, as tearing live scales causes infections.

crested-gecko.name: Crested Gecko
crested-gecko.tips: Usually sheds overnight and consumes the entire skin before morning. Check tail tip and toe pads for stuck rings.

boa-constrictor.name: Boa Constrictor (BCI)
boa-constrictor.tips: Boas exhibit a prominent dull phase followed by bright pink ventral belly scales during the pre-blue cycle.

blue-tongue-skink.name: Blue-Tongued Skink
blue-tongue-skink.tips: Indonesian species require high humidity to prevent stuck shedding from strangulating and amputating tiny toe digits.

veiled-chameleon.name: Veiled / Panther Chameleon
veiled-chameleon.humidity: 80% morning misting with warm shower perch
veiled-chameleon.tips: Explosive shedding! The entire skin 'pops' and flakes off in a white veil within 24–48 hours.

ui.profileSubtitle: Select species or customize your snake's biological profile.
ui.welfareRuleTitle: Modern Welfare Rule Applied (1.0 × Total Length)
ui.welfareRuleBody: Contemporary herpetological standards require the enclosure length to be at least equal to the snake's full body length. This allows the snake to stretch completely along one wall without curling, promoting joint health, digestive motility, and muscular tone.
ui.doorStyleBody: Front-sliding or swinging glass doors with sturdy safety key lock. Top-opening tanks can trigger predatory stress in snakes.
ui.escapeWarning: Snakes can squeeze through any gap wider than their skull!
ui.growthSubtitle: How your snake grows and when to upgrade vivarium size.
ui.babyNote: Babies need abundant clutter and snug hides to feel secure and feed reliably.
ui.juvenileNote: Rapid growth phase. Transition to larger adult food items and sturdy branches.
ui.adultNote: Permanent forever home allowing full thermal and photoperiod regulation.
ui.diagramSubtitle: Visual setup guide showing heat gradient, hide locations, and enrichment zones.
ui.baskingSurfaceNote: Natural flat stone under basking lamp
ui.rule1Body: Snake needs at least 2 identical snug hides (1 warm, 1 cool) so it doesn't choose between security and temperature.
ui.rule2Body: Every heat source MUST be plugged into a digital dimming or pulse proportional thermostat.
ui.rule3Body: Place on cool side to prevent rapid bacteria proliferation and uncontrolled humidity spikes.
ui.checkerSubtitle: Enter your current or prospective tank dimensions to verify if it satisfies your snake's welfare needs.

checkMessage.optimal: This tank is generous and exceeds minimum welfare standards! Your snake will have ample space to stretch, thermoregulate, and thrive.
checkMessage.bare-minimum: Borderline / Bare minimum. It will work temporarily, but upgrading to the recommended size is advised for natural behavior.
checkMessage.too-small: Too small for this snake. Snakes in undersized tanks suffer from obesity, spinal kinks, respiratory issues, and chronic stress.

ui.ingestedTitle: If your pet just ingested something:
ui.noMatches: Nothing matches — but if it's not in this list, still call poison control.

chocolate.name: Chocolate
chocolate.action: Call vet or ASPCA Poison Control (888-426-4435). Dark & baker's chocolate most dangerous.

grapes-raisins.name: Grapes / raisins
grapes-raisins.symptoms: Vomiting, lethargy, acute kidney failure within 24–72 h
grapes-raisins.action: Emergency vet immediately — no safe dose exists.

xylitol.name: Xylitol
xylitol.symptoms: Hypoglycemia within 30 min, liver failure within 24 h
xylitol.action: Emergency vet NOW. Found in sugar-free gum, peanut butter, toothpaste.

onion-garlic-chives.name: Onion / garlic / chives
onion-garlic-chives.symptoms: Weakness, pale gums, dark urine (hemolytic anemia)
onion-garlic-chives.action: Call vet — cats far more sensitive than dogs.

macadamia-nuts.name: Macadamia nuts
macadamia-nuts.symptoms: Weakness in hind legs, tremors, hyperthermia
macadamia-nuts.action: Usually self-limits in 24–48 h but call vet.

ibuprofen-advil.name: Ibuprofen (Advil)
ibuprofen-advil.action: Emergency vet — even one pill can be fatal to a cat.

acetaminophen-tylenol.name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol)
acetaminophen-tylenol.symptoms: Brown gums, difficulty breathing, liver failure
acetaminophen-tylenol.action: Emergency vet. Cats lack the enzyme to metabolize it.

antifreeze-ethylene-glycol.name: Antifreeze (ethylene glycol)
antifreeze-ethylene-glycol.symptoms: Drunken gait, then kidney failure within 24–72 h
antifreeze-ethylene-glycol.action: Emergency vet within 3 hours — antidote is time-critical.

lily-easter-tiger-asiatic.name: Lily (Easter, Tiger, Asiatic)
lily-easter-tiger-asiatic.symptoms: Vomiting, lethargy, kidney failure within 24–72 h
lily-easter-tiger-asiatic.action: Emergency vet — even pollen or vase water can kill a cat.

sago-palm.name: Sago palm
sago-palm.action: Emergency vet — 50%+ mortality even with treatment.

rodenticide.name: Rodenticide
rodenticide.action: Emergency vet — bring packaging so vet identifies active ingredient.

marijuana-thc.name: Marijuana / THC
marijuana-thc.symptoms: Wobbly gait, dilated pupils, urine dribbling
marijuana-thc.action: Vet — recovery usually 12–24 h; edibles with chocolate/xylitol more dangerous.

caffeine.name: Caffeine
caffeine.action: Vet if a coffee grounds / tea / caffeine pill ingestion.

bleach-concentrated.name: Bleach (concentrated)
bleach-concentrated.action: Rinse mouth with water/milk — do NOT induce vomiting. Call poison control.

ibuprofen-gel-patch.name: Ibuprofen gel / patch
ibuprofen-gel-patch.symptoms: Kidney damage from skin contact or chewing

alcohol.name: Alcohol
alcohol.action: Emergency vet — even mouthwash or raw bread dough (fermenting) is dangerous.

raw-yeast-dough.name: Raw yeast dough
raw-yeast-dough.symptoms: Bloated abdomen, alcohol toxicity, GI rupture

essential-oils-tea-tree-peppermint-pine.name: Essential oils (tea tree, peppermint, pine)
essential-oils-tea-tree-peppermint-pine.action: Wash off skin, vet visit. Cats extremely sensitive.

fertilizer-with-iron-insecticide.name: Fertilizer (with iron/insecticide)
fertilizer-with-iron-insecticide.action: Call poison control with product name.

pet-blood-test-explainer.name: Pet Blood Test Result Explainer
pet-blood-test-explainer.description: Enter your dog or cat's CBC and chemistry results and get plain-language explanations of any abnormal values. Covers 12 key parameters with dog/cat reference ranges and common causes of high or low results.

ui.enterHint: Enter only what appears on your report. Blank rows are skipped.
ui.emptyHint: Enter one or more values from your report to see what they mean.
ui.discussNote: Discuss these with your vet — a single out-of-range value is often meaningless without the full clinical picture.

pet-personality-quiz.name: Pet Personality Quiz
pet-personality-quiz.description: Answer 10 quick questions about how your dog or cat behaves at home, at play, and around new people. We match the pattern of answers to one of five personality archetypes — Adventurer, Companion, Free Spirit, Entertainer, or Zen Master — with practical training and enrichment tips for each type.

ui.answerAllHint: Answer all {{count}} questions to see the result.

quiz.q0: How does your pet greet you at the door?
quiz.q0o2: Looks up, then goes back to napping
quiz.q2: At the park or with new people, they…
quiz.q3o3: Brings it to you to share

which-breed-suits-me.name: Which Breed Suits Me? Quiz
which-breed-suits-me.description: Tell us your activity level, home size, grooming tolerance, and household setup — we score 13+ popular dog and cat breeds against your profile and return the five most likely to fit. A starting point before you meet individual animals at a shelter or breeder.

ui.suggestionsNote: These are starting suggestions — always meet individual animals before adopting; personality varies within any breed.

pet-compatibility-test.name: Pet Compatibility Test
pet-compatibility-test.description: Enter the species, age, temperament, sex, and neuter status of both pets and get a 0–100 compatibility score with a clear recommendation. Helpful when you're thinking about adding a second pet or introducing rescues to a resident animal.

band.likely: Likely to work with slow intros
band.highRisk: High risk — reconsider or consult a behaviorist

ui.introNote: Introductions matter more than any score. Use scent swapping, gated meets, and short supervised sessions over 1–2 weeks.

human-to-pet-age.name: Human Age → Pet Age (Reverse)
human-to-pet-age.description: Enter your human age and we run the standard pet-aging table in reverse to tell you how old you'd be as a small, medium, or large dog — or as a cat. A fun social-share tool built on the same veterinary-approved curves used in our forward age calculators.

ui.reverseNote: Reverse of standard pet-age tables. Real aging depends on breed and individual health.

pet-zodiac-birthday-card.name: Pet Zodiac & Birthday Card Generator
pet-zodiac-birthday-card.description: Enter your pet's name and birthday to reveal their Western zodiac sign with a fun personality blurb, then print a shareable birthday card. Great for social posts and adoption anniversaries.

pisces.traits: Gentle, intuitive, deeply bonded to their people.

pet-name-meaning-lookup.name: Pet Name Meaning Lookup
pet-name-meaning-lookup.description: Search 25+ of the most popular dog and cat names to see their linguistic origin, literal meaning, and personality vibe. Helpful when you're deciding between shortlisted names or want a story to tell friends about the name you picked.

adoption-vs-buying-cost-comparator.name: Adoption vs Buying Cost Comparator
adoption-vs-buying-cost-comparator.description: Compare the true first-year cost of adopting a pet from a shelter versus buying from a breeder or pet store. Adoption fees typically include spay/neuter, core vaccines, and microchipping — services that add $500-$800 when you buy a pet elsewhere. Enter local prices to get a personalized side-by-side breakdown of both paths and see the real dollar difference before you bring a pet home.

ui.savingsNote: Plus you give a home to a pet in need. Ongoing costs (food, insurance, vet) are the same either way.

litter-size-predictor.name: Litter Size Predictor
litter-size-predictor.description: Predict how many puppies, kittens, or rabbit kits to expect in a litter based on breed size category, the mother's age, and how many times she has bred before. Litter size varies widely — a Chihuahua averages 3 puppies while a Great Dane may deliver 12 — and first-time mothers typically produce fewer offspring than experienced dams in their prime. Use this as an educational planning estimate before your reproductive veterinarian confirms the count with ultrasound or X-ray.

litterNote.rabbit: Rabbit kindles vary widely by breed

ui.breedNote: First litters usually run below breed average. Prime reproductive age is 2-5 years, after which litter sizes gradually decline. Ultrasound at day 25-30 and X-ray at day 55 give the only accurate count — this estimator is educational only.
ui.breedingWarning: Responsible breeding requires health testing, veterinary supervision, and a plan for every puppy or kitten. Consult a reproductive veterinarian before breeding.

clicker-training-planner.name: Clicker Training Planner
clicker-training-planner.description: Clicker training is the gold standard of modern, force-free animal learning. The click sound becomes a precise marker your pet learns to trust — it says 'that exact behavior earned you a treat.' This planner walks you through the six-phase timeline used by professional trainers: charging the clicker, capturing behaviors, luring, adding cue words, proofing under distraction, and finally thinning food rewards. It works for dogs, cats, parrots, rabbits, ferrets, and even horses, and it produces cleaner learning than voice-only markers because it eliminates tone variation and body-language noise.

ui.phaseChargeDesc: Click + treat 20 times with no expectation. Pet learns click = food.
ui.phaseCaptureDesc: Click the moment your pet sits, lies down, or looks at you naturally.
ui.phaseLureDesc: Guide with a treat, click at success, then fade the lure over 10 reps.
ui.phaseCueDesc: Say the word right before the behavior, then click + treat when it happens.
ui.phaseProofDesc: Practice in the yard, on walks, and around distractions.
ui.phaseReduceDesc: Move to variable reinforcement: reward every 2-3 correct responses.
ui.sessionsHint: 3-5 minute sessions, 2-4x daily, work best for most pets.
ui.totalSessions: Total sessions to solid cue response: ≈ {{count}} short sessions over 30 days.

potty-training-schedule.name: Potty Training Schedule
potty-training-schedule.description: House training is the number-one reason puppies get returned to shelters — and it's almost always fixable with better scheduling. Puppies can hold their bladder for roughly their age-in-months in hours (a 3-month-old holds ~3 hours), and they need to go out after every meal, nap, play session, and training block. This tool builds a personalized daily schedule from your puppy's age and your household's wake/bedtime hours, so you can post it on the fridge and stop guessing.

ui.triggerPlay: After every play or training session
ui.triggerCrate: Before crate time and before bed

crate-training-timeline.name: Crate Training Timeline
crate-training-timeline.description: Done well, the crate is one of the most valuable tools in modern dog training — it accelerates house training, keeps puppies safe when unsupervised, and gives adult dogs a portable den for travel and vet stays. Done poorly, it creates lifelong panic and barrier frustration. This timeline follows the standard veterinary behavior progression: three weeks of gradual desensitization from 'crate is a magical treat dispenser' to 'sleeps peacefully overnight and during your workday.' Rushing this timeline is the single biggest cause of crate hate.

ui.detailIntroduce: Door open, treats and toys inside. Never force.
ui.detailMeals: Feed all meals in the crate with door open.
ui.detailCloseDoor: Close for 30 sec while eating, reopen calmly.
ui.detailStays: You in the room, calm praise on quiet.
ui.detailLeave: Step out 5-30 min, ignore whining, reward silence.
ui.detailAbsences: Short errands (30-60 min). Puppies max 3-4 hours.
ui.detailOvernight: Adult dogs max 6-8 hours; puppies need midday break.
ui.intro: A 3-week desensitization plan. Never use the crate as punishment.

leash-training-progress.name: Leash Training Progress
leash-training-progress.description: A dog that pulls on leash isn't 'stubborn' — they're simply on a schedule of continuous reinforcement, because every step of pulling gets them where they want to go. Loose-leash walking is a trained skill built one criterion at a time: first indoors, then in the yard, then around distractions. This tracker lists the ten measurable milestones that certified trainers use, from 'wears the leash calmly indoors' to 'passes another dog under threshold.' Tick each one as you go and progress persists on your device.

ui.m1: Wears collar & leash indoors without fuss
ui.m2: Follows me across the living room
ui.m3: Walks 5 min in the yard without pulling
ui.m6: Loose leash for a full 10-minute walk
ui.intro: Tick milestones as your dog masters them. Progress saves to this device.

recall-training-tracker.name: Recall Training Tracker
recall-training-tracker.description: Recall — coming when called — is the most important behavior any pet will learn, and the hardest to build reliably. This tracker lets you log every recall attempt across environments, from indoors to busy parks, so you can watch your reliability percentage grow over time. Certified trainers use the '90% rule': you should not trust your dog off-leash in unfenced areas until they hit 90%+ reliability across at least 20 sessions in that environment. Guessing your dog's reliability without data is why so many pets are lost each year.

ui.targetHint: Target 90%+ before trusting off-leash in unfenced areas.
ui.emptyState: Log your first session to start tracking.

socialization-checklist.name: Puppy Socialization Checklist
socialization-checklist.description: The socialization window closes between 12-16 weeks of age — after that, novelty exposure creates suspicion instead of confidence. A puppy who meets 100 friendly people, calmly experiences 50 environments, and hears 30 unusual sounds before 16 weeks grows into a stable adult dog. A puppy that only meets family and other dogs grows into a reactive, fearful adult that costs thousands in behavior consultants. This checklist covers the five categories AVSAB recommends: people, animals, environments, surfaces & sounds, and handling.

ui.intro: Aim to expose your puppy positively to 100 new things before 16 weeks.

puppy-milestone-tracker.name: Puppy Milestone Tracker
puppy-milestone-tracker.description: Puppy development follows a predictable timeline — eyes open at week 3, adult teeth erupt around week 16, and hormonal maturity arrives between 6-12 months depending on breed size. Missing a milestone by more than 1-2 weeks warrants a veterinary check-in. This tracker lists the ten most important developmental checkpoints, each with the typical week it occurs and what to watch for. Tick them off as they happen and keep this list handy for vet visits.

ui.w8: Ready to go home; first vaccine
ui.w16: Third vaccine + rabies; adult teeth erupting
ui.intro: Standard puppy developmental checkpoints. Confirm timing with your veterinarian.

aggression-risk-assessment.name: Aggression Risk Assessment
aggression-risk-assessment.description: Aggression in pets is almost always fear-based and predictable — most bites are preceded by weeks or months of warning signs that owners miss or minimize. This screening tool walks through eight evidence-based risk factors used by certified veterinary behaviorists: resource guarding, freezing, hard stares, snapping, and bite history. It does not diagnose aggression, but it flags whether you should seek professional help. Any positive answer to a bite-history question warrants immediate consultation with a veterinary behaviorist (Dip ACVB).

ui.q1: Stiffens or freezes when approached while eating
ui.q4: Reacts intensely to other dogs on leash
ui.q5: Guards toys, food bowl, or resting spot
ui.q6: Shows a hard stare at strangers
ui.q7: Snaps in the air as a warning
ui.safetyNote: Safety first. This screening tool does not diagnose aggression. Any bite history, resource guarding, or unpredictable reactivity requires evaluation by a certified veterinary behaviorist (Dip ACVB) or a certified behavior consultant (CDBC / IAABC). Rule out pain and thyroid disease with your veterinarian first — medical issues cause many "sudden" aggression cases.

separation-anxiety-score.name: Separation Anxiety Score
separation-anxiety-score.description: Separation-related distress affects 20-40% of pet dogs and is one of the most misunderstood behavior problems. It is not 'being spoiled' or 'acting out' — it is a genuine panic disorder that resembles a human panic attack. Dogs experiencing it can urinate, destroy doors, or injure themselves within minutes of being left alone. This assessment scores eight validated indicators from the Overall/CSAT screening framework and provides a severity band: minimal, mild, moderate, or severe. Mild cases often respond to enrichment and slow absence training; moderate to severe cases benefit from medication and specialist support.

ui.q3: House soils only when alone (fully trained)
ui.q4: Follows you room to room constantly
ui.q6: Excessive drooling or pacing when alone
ui.q7: Won't eat treats or food while alone
ui.adviceNote: Mild cases respond to counter-conditioning and enrichment. Moderate to severe cases benefit from a certified separation-anxiety trainer (CSAT) and, in many cases, medication prescribed by your veterinarian. Do not use punishment or "cry it out" methods — they worsen panic.

trick-training-library.name: Trick Training Library
trick-training-library.description: Trick training is more than a party trick — it builds focus, exercises the brain, and strengthens the human-animal bond. Ten minutes of trick training tires most dogs more than an hour of walking. This library lists eleven classic tricks organized by difficulty, from 'Sit' to 'Put toys away,' each with the exact luring and shaping steps used by professional trainers. Filter by level to find your next challenge, and remember: every trick is trained in tiny increments, not one big leap.

ui.trickSitSteps: Lure nose up until rear touches floor, click, treat. Add cue after 10 reps.
ui.trickDownSteps: From sit, lure straight down to floor between paws.
ui.trickShakeSteps: Tickle back of paw, click when it lifts. Add hand cue.
ui.trickSpinSteps: Lure nose in a circle. Fade lure to a finger point.
ui.trickRolloverSteps: From down, lure nose over shoulder toward hip.
ui.trickBowSteps: Capture the play bow, mark with clicker, name it.
ui.trickSpeakSteps: Capture a bark on cue, then reward silence to teach 'quiet'.
ui.trickFetchSteps: Trade a toy for a treat; only reward when placed in your hand.
ui.trickWeaveSteps: Lure through leg → step → lure back. Chain into figure-8.
ui.trickPlaydeadSteps: From roll-over, add finger-gun cue, wait 3 seconds before release.
ui.trickTidySteps: Chain 'take it' + 'drop it' over a bin. Reward the release into bin.

command-vocabulary-builder.name: Command Vocabulary Builder
command-vocabulary-builder.description: The average pet dog understands 165 words; exceptional dogs learn 1,000+ (Chaser the Border Collie learned 1,022 nouns in controlled studies). Every cue you teach is a fresh channel of communication that reduces frustration on both sides. This builder starts with five foundational commands (Sit, Down, Come, Stay, Leave it) and lets you add unlimited new cues with their meanings. Tick off which are mastered and see your total vocabulary grow — a wonderful record to bring to every vet or trainer visit.

behavior-journal.name: Pet Behavior Journal
behavior-journal.description: Most behavior 'mysteries' aren't mysteries — they're patterns waiting to be seen. Journaling for two weeks reveals what actually triggers your pet's barking, growling, or anxiety, versus what you assume triggers it. This journal captures the ABC of behavior science: Antecedent (what happened right before), Behavior (what your pet did), and Consequence (your response). Add a note field for context. Bring the last 30 entries to your veterinary behaviorist or trainer — the pattern often reveals the diagnosis before words do.

ui.emptyState: Consistent journaling reveals patterns — most owners spot the trigger cluster within 2 weeks.

reward-schedule-calculator.name: Reward Schedule Calculator
reward-schedule-calculator.description: When to reward — and how often — is what separates trained dogs from dogs who only work if they see a treat. Continuous reinforcement (reward every rep) is essential during learning but destroys reliability if kept forever. Variable reinforcement (reward unpredictably) is what makes trained behaviors permanent — the same principle that makes slot machines addictive. This tool tells you exactly what reinforcement schedule to use for each training stage: acquisition, fluency, generalization, or maintenance.

ui.noteAcquisition: Reward every correct response while pet is learning the behavior.
ui.noteFluency: Reward on average every 3rd rep — builds speed and reliability.
ui.noteGeneralization: In new environments, jackpot occasional big rewards. Keep verbal praise every time.
ui.noteMaintenance: Behavior is a lifestyle — reward once every 8-10 reps or after harder repetitions.
ui.ruleNote: Rule: weaken rewards too fast and the behavior extinguishes. If reliability drops below 80%, back up one stage for a few days before thinning the schedule again.

barking-log.name: Barking Log
barking-log.description: Excessive barking is the number-one complaint neighbors report to animal control — and the number-one reason dogs are surrendered to shelters. But 'excessive barking' is rarely one problem; it's usually 3-4 different triggers running on the same pattern. This log lets you record every notable bark event with its trigger and duration, then automatically ranks your top triggers so you can address the biggest one first. Two weeks of logging usually reveals the culprit that's driving 60-80% of the barking.

litter-training-planner.name: Litter Training Planner (Cats & Rabbits)
litter-training-planner.description: Cats and rabbits are two of the easiest species to litter train — they instinctively prefer a consistent bathroom spot — but the setup is completely different for each. Cats need unscented clumping litter in a low-traffic box with the '1 per cat + 1' rule. Rabbits need paper-based litter, hay on top, and never clumping clay (which is toxic if ingested). This planner walks through the 3-week timeline for each species, from first setup to reliable free-roam privileges. Regression after training is usually medical (UTI, stones) — not behavioral.

ui.catStep1: Set up 1 box per cat +1 in a quiet, low-traffic spot. Use unscented clumping litter, 3 inches deep.
ui.catStep23: Place kitten in box after meals and naps. Praise calmly if they dig or eliminate.
ui.catStep47: Scoop twice daily. Never punish accidents — clean with enzymatic cleaner to remove scent markers.
ui.catStepW2: If accidents continue, add a second box near the accident location.
ui.catStepW34: Slowly transition litter type if needed (mix 25% new / 75% old for 3 days, then 50/50, then 100%).
ui.rabbitStep1: Place a corner litter box inside the enclosure. Use paper-based litter (never clumping/clay).
ui.rabbitStep23: Add a handful of hay on top — rabbits naturally chew and poop while eating.
ui.rabbitStep47: Move any stray droppings into the box to reinforce the scent location.
ui.rabbitStepW2: Once 80% of droppings land in the box, allow supervised free-roam.
ui.rabbitStepW3p: Spay/neuter around 4-6 months dramatically improves litter reliability.
ui.vetNote: Sudden loss of litter-box habits often signals a UTI, bladder stones, or arthritis. Any regression lasting more than 3 days warrants a vet visit.

heat-cycle-tracker.name: Heat Cycle Tracker (Dog, Cat, Rabbit)
heat-cycle-tracker.description: Understanding your intact female's heat cycle is essential whether you're breeding intentionally or simply avoiding unwanted litters. This tracker records each observed stage — proestrus, estrus, diestrus, anestrus — and estimates the next expected cycle based on species-typical intervals: roughly every 6 months for dogs, every 2-3 weeks during breeding season for cats, and continuously receptive (induced ovulator) for rabbits. Consistent logging helps identify silent heats, split heats, prolonged bleeding, and pyometra risk factors long before they become emergencies.

ui.dogNote: Most dogs cycle every 6 months. Small breeds sometimes every 4, giants every 12-18.
ui.catNote: Cats are seasonally polyestrous — they cycle every 2-3 weeks during breeding season (spring–fall).
ui.rabbitNote: Rabbits are induced ovulators — no true heat cycle; they can conceive nearly any day.
ui.emptyState: No entries yet — log your first observation.

pregnancy-calendar.name: Pregnancy Calendar (Species-Specific)
pregnancy-calendar.description: Enter the mating date and pick your species — dog, cat, rabbit, guinea pig, hamster, ferret, horse, goat, or sheep — and get a personalized pregnancy calendar with due date, trimester markers, vet-check milestones, and nesting-prep deadlines. Dogs (63 days), cats (65 days), rabbits (31 days), horses (340 days) — each species has a distinct gestation length and a different rhythm of physical and behavioral changes. Knowing what to expect week by week is the difference between a smooth delivery and a preventable emergency.

ui.dogM21: Nipples enlarge, appetite may drop briefly
ui.dogM55: Set up whelping box, isolate mom
ui.dogM60: Rectal temp 2x daily — drop below 99°F = 24h to labor
ui.catM58: Set up kittening box in quiet room
ui.genEarly: Early gestation — normal diet, gentle handling
ui.trimesterNote: First trimester ends {{week1}} · nesting prep by {{nesting}}

whelping-kittening-checklist.name: Whelping / Kittening Prep Checklist
whelping-kittening-checklist.description: The two weeks before a litter arrives are when most preventable problems are avoided. This checklist walks through every physical item you need in your whelping kit, how to set up a proper whelping or kittening box, what to discuss with your vet at the 55-day check, and the critical postpartum monitoring window (colostrum, weight, mom's temperature). Skip any of these steps and a routine birth can turn into an emergency at 2 a.m.

ui.groupBox: Whelping box setup (2-3 weeks before due date)
ui.box1: Sturdy whelping box 1.5x mom's body length, with pig rails to prevent crushing
ui.box2: Newspaper base + clean towels/vet-bed on top
ui.box3: Heat lamp or heating pad set to 85-90°F for first week (one warm corner only)
ui.box4: Quiet, low-traffic room where mom feels safe
ui.box5: Introduce mom to the box 7-10 days early so she claims it
ui.kit3: Unscented dental floss for tying umbilical cords
ui.kit5: Iodine or chlorhexidine for cord stumps
ui.kit6: Digital scale (gram accuracy) for daily weigh-ins
ui.kit10: Notebook + pen — log time of birth, weight, sex, markings
ui.vet2: X-ray at day 45+ to confirm puppy/kitten count
ui.vet3: Emergency vet phone number posted on the wall
ui.vet4: Know the address of the nearest 24-hour ER vet
ui.vet5: Learn signs of dystocia: >2h active straining with no birth, >4h between births, green discharge before first pup
ui.vet6: Discuss C-section threshold with your vet in advance
ui.post1: Confirm each newborn nurses within 2 hours (colostrum window)
ui.post2: Weigh every newborn daily — no weight loss beyond day 2
ui.post3: Check mom's temperature 2x daily for 5 days (>103°F = infection risk)
ui.post4: Watch for retained placenta, mastitis, eclampsia (milk fever)
ui.post5: Keep visitors away for 2 weeks — stress can trigger cannibalism or rejection

stud-fee-calculator.name: Stud Fee Calculator
stud-fee-calculator.description: Pricing a stud fee correctly is one of the harder decisions in ethical breeding. Undercharge and you devalue your stud's line; overcharge and quality bitches go elsewhere. This calculator uses the industry-standard formula — average puppy price × stud quality multiplier — to suggest a fair cash fee, and compares it to a pick-of-litter arrangement. Pet-quality males typically fetch 40% of one puppy price, titled dogs 100%, champions 150%, and proven top producers with imported bloodlines 200%+.

ui.cashNote: Industry norm: 1 puppy price for titled studs, up to 2x for champions.
ui.pickNote: Stud owner selects 1st pick after the breeder's own retention.
ui.contractNote: Always use a written stud contract. Cover: repeat breeding rights if litter fails, health-test requirements, payment timing, and pick order.

genetic-diversity-calculator.name: Genetic Diversity / COI Calculator
genetic-diversity-calculator.description: The Coefficient of Inbreeding (COI) is the single most important number in ethical breeding decisions. It measures how genetically similar the sire and dam are — the higher the number, the greater the risk that hidden recessive diseases will express in the litter. This calculator gives a quick estimate based on shared ancestors and generations back, plus context on what each COI band means (0-6.25% ideal, 25%+ full-sibling level and dangerous). For final decisions, always run a full 10-generation pedigree COI through breed-club or veterinary software.

ui.noteLow: Similar to unrelated pairing. Healthy diversity.
ui.noteModerate: Comparable to first-cousin pairing. Acceptable if health tests are clean.
ui.noteHigh: Half-sibling equivalent. Reduced litter vigor and immune diversity likely.
ui.noteVeryHigh: Full-sibling / parent-offspring pairing. Not recommended — strong risk of recessive disease expression.
ui.ancestorsLabel: Number of shared ancestors within pedigree
ui.pedigreeHint: Full 5-generation pedigrees give the most reliable estimate.
ui.accurateNote: For accurate pedigree-based COI, use software like Breedmate or the breed database's COI calculator with a full 10-generation pedigree.

puppy-kitten-weight-chart.name: Puppy & Kitten Weight Chart
puppy-kitten-weight-chart.description: In the first four weeks of life, weight is the single most reliable indicator of a newborn's health. Puppies and kittens should gain 5-10% of their body weight every day — a plateau of even 12 hours is a genuine emergency. This tracker logs every weigh-in (grams, not ounces — accuracy matters at this stage), plots gain since the previous session, and flags any stagnation. Reference ranges are conservative averages; small toy breeds and giant breeds will fall well outside typical numbers, so trend matters more than absolute weight.

ui.gainWarning: — 🚨 Weight loss or stagnation in a neonate is an emergency. Call your vet.

weaning-schedule.name: Weaning Schedule (Puppies, Kittens, Rabbits)
weaning-schedule.description: Weaning is a gradual process, not a switch. Puppies and kittens should be introduced to solid food around week 3-4, transitioned over 3-5 weeks, and fully weaned by week 7-8 — but they should stay with mom and littermates for social development until at least 8-10 weeks (puppies) or 10-12 weeks (kittens). Rabbit kits follow a different rhythm: alfalfa-based diet only, greens delayed until well after weaning. This tool builds a species-specific week-by-week plan from the litter's birth date.

ui.puppyD3: Introduce puppy gruel: soaked kibble + puppy milk replacer, 4x daily. Nursing still primary.
ui.puppyD4: Thicker gruel, less milk replacer. Puppies eating solids ~30% of intake.
ui.puppyD5: Soaked kibble only (no milk replacer). Nursing 2-3x daily.
ui.puppyD6: Dry kibble + water on side. Nursing reduced to 1-2x daily.
ui.puppyD7: Fully on solid puppy food. Separate mom for longer periods.
ui.puppyD8: Weaning complete. Ready to leave litter (US minimum; 10 weeks better).
ui.kittenD4: Introduce wet food gruel (kitten formula + KMR). 4x daily, small amounts.
ui.kittenD5: Thicker wet food. Kittens tasting more solids.
ui.kittenD6: Full wet kitten food, dry kibble available. Nursing reduces.
ui.kittenD8: Weaning complete. Do NOT rehome before 10-12 weeks (social development).
ui.rabbitD34: Kits nibble mom's pellets and hay. Do not offer greens yet.
ui.rabbitD56: Free-fed alfalfa hay and alfalfa-based pellets.
ui.rabbitD78: Fully weaned. Introduce small amounts of leafy greens one at a time.
ui.summary: Weaning starts week {{start}}, complete by week {{end}}. Do not rehome before minimum age.

newborn-care-timeline.name: Newborn Care Timeline
newborn-care-timeline.description: The first 12 weeks of a puppy or kitten's life have more milestones than any other period. Colostrum in the first 2 hours, eyes opening around day 10-14, first solid food at 3-4 weeks, first vaccines at 6-8 weeks, socialization windows that close forever if missed. This timeline lays out every stage from day 0 to rehoming, with the tasks a breeder or foster caregiver needs to complete at each step. Follow it closely — the difference between a well-adjusted puppy or kitten and a problem adult is set in these weeks.

ui.colostrum1: Confirm all newborns nurse within 2 hours
ui.colostrum2: Weigh at birth, then every 12h for 3 days
ui.colostrum3: Room temp 85-90°F for puppies, 88°F for kittens
ui.colostrum4: Watch for fading — cold, limp, or crying constantly = emergency vet
ui.adjustment2: Cord stumps fall off around day 3
ui.adjustment4: Deworm mom (safe wormer only) — nematodes pass through milk
ui.movements2: Introduce a shallow litter tray (kittens) or paper (puppies)
ui.movements4: Begin gentle handling — 30 sec per pup, 3-4x daily
ui.weaning3: Nails trimmed weekly (mom's teats get scratched)
ui.independence3: Socialization with humans — new sounds, gentle handling
ui.rehome4: Provide new owners with weight/vaccine/deworming records
ui.emergencyNote: Emergency signs: constant crying, cold to touch, no weight gain by day 2, refusing to nurse, blue/pale gums. Call an emergency vet immediately — neonates crash within hours.

heatstroke-risk-calculator.name: Heatstroke Risk Calculator
heatstroke-risk-calculator.description: Combine temperature, humidity, coat type, breed and activity level to estimate real-time heatstroke risk and get vet-informed guidance on outdoor exposure.

ui.adviceLow: Normal outdoor time is fine. Always provide shade and fresh water.
ui.adviceExtreme: Keep indoors with AC. Even brief exposure risks fatal heatstroke, especially for flat-faced or senior pets.
ui.adviceHigh: Limit outdoors to bathroom breaks only. Walk before sunrise or after sunset. Watch for excessive panting, drooling, or wobbliness.
ui.adviceModerate: Shorten walks, avoid pavement, carry water, take shade breaks every 10 minutes.
ui.seniorLabel: Senior or has heart / respiratory condition
ui.emergencyNote: Emergency signs: heavy panting, bright red gums, drooling ropes of saliva, vomiting, collapse. Cool with room-temperature (not ice) water on paws/belly and drive to the ER immediately.

cold-weather-safety-score.name: Cold Weather Safety Score
cold-weather-safety-score.description: Wind chill, coat type, size and wetness combine into a personalized cold-weather safety score with clear guidance on frostbite and hypothermia risk.

ui.adviceSafe: Normal outdoor time. Watch for lifted paws — that's the first sign your pet is cold.
ui.adviceExtreme: Bathroom breaks only, under 5 minutes. Frostbite risk on ears, tail, paws. Use boots and an insulated coat.
ui.adviceDanger: Limit to short outings (10-15 min). Coat and booties recommended for small or short-coated pets.
ui.adviceChilly: Small or short-haired dogs benefit from a sweater. Keep walks brisk to maintain body heat.
ui.puppyLabel: Puppy, senior, or thin body condition
ui.hypoNote: Hypothermia signs: shivering, weakness, slow breathing, pale gums. Warm gradually with blankets and call your vet.

paw-pad-temperature-checker.name: Paw Pad Temperature Checker
paw-pad-temperature-checker.description: Estimate ground surface temperature from air temp, surface material and sun exposure — plus the maximum safe contact time before burns occur.

ui.labelCaution: Uncomfortable — will burn on prolonged contact
ui.testNote: 7-second test: place the back of your hand on the ground. If you can't hold it for 7 seconds, it's too hot for paws. Walk on grass, in shade, or use boots.

fireworks-anxiety-prep.name: Fireworks Anxiety Prep
fireworks-anxiety-prep.description: Step-by-step checklist covering desensitization, environment setup, safe hideaways, and emergency planning to help firework-fearful pets cope.

ui.week1: Ask vet about calming meds (Sileo, trazodone) if severe
ui.week2: Order a pressure wrap (Thundershirt) if new
ui.week3: Start playing low-volume firework sounds during meals to desensitize
ui.week4: Update microchip and ID tag — most lost-pet reports spike on July 4
ui.day1: Long walk / exercise in the morning to burn energy
ui.day2: Feed dinner early before noise starts
ui.day3: Take a final potty break before dusk
ui.day4: Close all windows, blinds, and doors
ui.day5: Set up a den: covered crate or interior bathroom with bedding
ui.during1: Turn on white noise, TV, or classical music
ui.during2: Stay calm — pets mirror your energy
ui.during3: Offer a high-value chew or lick mat
ui.during4: Don't punish hiding — let them retreat
ui.during5: Never take pets to firework displays
ui.emergency2: Recent photo on your phone for lost-pet posters
ui.emergency3: Neighbors know your pet in case of escape

halloween-safety-checker.name: Halloween Safety Checker
halloween-safety-checker.description: Look up chocolate, candy, costumes, glow sticks and more to see which Halloween items are toxic, hazardous or just cautionary for pets.

ui.dChocolate: Dark and baking chocolate most dangerous. Even small amounts cause vomiting, tremors, seizures.
ui.dXylitol: Extremely toxic to dogs — causes rapid hypoglycemia and liver failure. Even one piece can be fatal.
ui.dRaisins: Cause acute kidney failure in dogs. Common in trick-or-treat mix.
ui.dWrappers: Foreign body obstruction risk; often need surgery.
ui.dGlow: Bitter-tasting fluid causes drooling and mouth foaming (rarely fatal but distressing).
ui.dCostumes: Never leave a costumed pet unsupervised. Check nothing restricts breathing, vision, or movement.
ui.dDoor: Trick-or-treaters mean constant door opening — biggest cause of lost pets on Halloween.
ui.dCandles: Curious tails and paws can knock over open flames.
ui.dBlackCats: Keep indoor-only for the week around Halloween due to cruelty risk.
ui.searchPlaceholder: Search a Halloween item (chocolate, costume, glow stick…)
ui.emergencyNote: Emergency: ASPCA Animal Poison Control 1-888-426-4435 (fee applies). Call your ER vet immediately if ingestion is suspected.

christmas-hazard-lookup.name: Christmas Hazard Lookup
christmas-hazard-lookup.description: A veterinary-informed database of Christmas-season dangers — from poinsettia and tinsel to turkey bones and holiday alcohol — with severity ratings and safety advice.

ui.dPoinsettia: Mildly toxic — mouth irritation and drooling. Rarely serious but keep out of reach.
ui.dHolly: Berries cause vomiting, diarrhea, and cardiovascular effects with mistletoe.
ui.dLilies: Deadly to cats — any part causes acute kidney failure. Even pollen or vase water.
ui.dTreeWater: May contain fertilizer, bacteria, or preservatives — cover the base.
ui.dTinsel: Linear foreign body — cats love it; nearly always requires surgery if swallowed.
ui.dOrnaments: Cuts to mouth, paws, or GI tract. Hang fragile ornaments high.
ui.dLights: Chewing causes electrical burns and shock. Unplug when unsupervised.
ui.dChocolate: Rich holiday foods = pancreatitis. Chocolate and macadamia especially dangerous.
ui.dOnions: In stuffing and gravy — cause hemolytic anemia in dogs and cats.
ui.dAlcohol: Even eggnog and rum cake are dangerous. Rapid drop in blood sugar and body temperature.
ui.dBones: Cooked bones splinter — GI perforation risk. Give raw carrots instead.
ui.dSnowGlobes: May contain antifreeze/ethylene glycol — deadly in tiny amounts.
ui.dCandles: Burns and fire risk from tails, jumping cats. Use flameless.
ui.dWrapping: GI obstruction if swallowed. Clean up promptly.
ui.poisonNote: Poison Control: ASPCA 1-888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline 1-855-764-7661.

allergy-season-tracker.name: Allergy Season Tracker
allergy-season-tracker.description: Track your pet's itch level, pollen index and symptoms day by day. Identify the worst weeks, spot food or environmental triggers, and share the log with your vet.

ui.notesPlaceholder: New food, bath, walked in tall grass…

air-quality-impact-assessor.name: Air Quality Impact Assessor
air-quality-impact-assessor.description: Enter the local AQI and pet profile to see whether it's safe to walk, exercise or leave your pet outdoors during smoke, smog and pollution events.

ui.actionNormal: Enjoy walks and outdoor play as usual.
ui.actionIndoors: Cancel all outdoor exercise. Run an air purifier. Keep windows closed. Birds especially vulnerable to particulate lung damage.
ui.actionBathroom: Skip walks and outdoor play. Watch for coughing or lethargy. Pets with heart or lung disease need extra caution.
ui.actionShorten: Cut walks in half. Avoid strenuous exercise. Wipe paws and coat after outings to remove particulates.
ui.sensitiveLabel: Senior, puppy, or has heart / lung condition
ui.warningNote: Warning signs: coughing, wheezing, watery eyes, reluctance to move, reduced appetite. Contact your vet if symptoms persist after 24h indoors.

reptile-uvb-schedule.name: Reptile UVB Schedule
reptile-uvb-schedule.description: Get species-specific UVB lighting hours, target UV Index, bulb type recommendations, and an automatic replacement date so your reptile never silently develops metabolic bone disease.

ui.noteBeardedDragon: Desert species — high UVB demand. Use T5-HO 10-12% linear bulb across ⅔ of the enclosure length.
ui.noteLeopardGecko: Crepuscular; low UVB (2-5% T5 or shade-dweller bulb) still improves bone health and behaviour.
ui.noteBallPython: Nocturnal — Arcadia ShadeDweller or 5% T5 improves circadian rhythm and vitamin D.
ui.noteCornSnake: Diurnal in the wild. 5-7% T5 helps immune function and colour.
ui.noteRussianTortoise: Grassland species — needs strong UVB. 10-12% T5-HO.
ui.noteSulcata: Arid grazer — 12% T5-HO or outdoor sunlight is ideal.
ui.noteRedEaredSlider: Aquatic. Mount UVB above the basking dock, not through glass.
ui.noteChameleon: Panther/Veiled — 6% T5-HO across the screen top; monitor with Solarmeter 6.5.
ui.noteBlueTongueSkink: Diurnal omnivore — 6% T5 across ½ enclosure.
ui.bulbLifeNote: Even when a UVB bulb still glows visibly, its UVB output drops sharply after the rated life — reptiles then develop metabolic bone disease silently.

tank-temperature-gradient-calculator.name: Tank Temperature Gradient Calculator
tank-temperature-gradient-calculator.description: Compare your reptile enclosure temperatures to species-correct basking, ambient, cool-zone and nighttime ranges — with plain-English warnings when a zone is dangerous.

ui.noteBeardedDragon: Never use heat rocks — surface burns are common.
ui.noteLeopardGecko: Belly heat is critical — use a DHP or under-tank heater on a thermostat.
ui.noteCrestedGecko: Sensitive to heat — above 85°F is dangerous.
ui.noteBallPython: Provide two identical hides on each side of the gradient.
ui.noteCornSnake: Cool side can safely drop into the 60s at night.
ui.noteRussianTortoise: Requires a strong day/night temperature drop.
ui.noteRedEaredSlider: Water 75-80°F; measure basking dock surface temp, not air.
ui.noteChameleon: Nighttime drop is essential — never heat the enclosure at night unless below 55°F.
ui.measureNote: Measure with an infrared temp gun at the actual surface — stick-on gauges lie.

bird-wing-clipping-guide.name: Bird Wing Clipping Guide
bird-wing-clipping-guide.description: Learn how many primary flight feathers to trim by species, why both wings must always be clipped equally, and when leaving your parrot flighted is actually the safer choice.

ui.flightedNote: Flighted is healthiest when the room is truly bird-proofed.
ui.warnBlood: Never clip: blood feathers (dark shafts), secondaries, coverts, or tail feathers.
ui.warnOneWing: Never clip only one wing — birds spin, crash and injure the keel.
ui.warnFledgling: Never clip fledglings — they must learn to fly for lifelong coordination.
ui.warnPro: Get professional help the first time. Wing clipping is educational information only, not a substitute for an avian vet or experienced groomer.
ui.notesBudgie: Very light — a small over-clip can prevent all glide.
ui.notesCockatiel: Leave a small gliding capability so a startled bird can descend safely instead of crashing.
ui.notesConure: Muscular fliers — under-clipping still leaves powerful lift.
ui.notesAmazon: Heavy body — avoid over-clip that causes hard falls.
ui.notesAfricanGrey: Prone to keel-bone injury from hard landings — leave glide capability.
ui.notesMacaw: Very heavy — many experts recommend leaving flighted with a harness instead of clipping.

ferret-litter-trainer.name: Ferret Litter Trainer
ferret-litter-trainer.description: Follow a proven 10-step plan to litter-train ferrets, track accidents to spot patterns, and set up multi-room boxes so your household stays clean-smelling.

ui.step1: Place a low corner litter box in each room your ferret plays in — ferrets rarely walk more than 2 metres to relieve themselves.
ui.step2: Use dust-free paper pellets or recycled newspaper pellets. Never clumping clay or pine/cedar shavings.
ui.step3: Confine to a small area (a cage or exercise pen) for the first 1-2 weeks to build the habit.
ui.step4: Every time your ferret starts backing into a corner, gently place them in the litter box.
ui.step5: Reward successful use immediately with a lickable meat treat (bacon fat, salmon oil, high-protein paste).
ui.step6: Clean accidents with an enzymatic cleaner (never ammonia — it smells like urine).
ui.step7: Slowly expand freedom room-by-room only after a full week of no accidents.
ui.step8: Add a second litter box in every new room you unlock.
ui.step9: Scoop 1-2 times daily; ferrets refuse dirty boxes and will pick a corner instead.
ui.step10: Expect 60-80% reliability — even trained ferrets occasionally miss. This is normal.
ui.tipNote: If accidents cluster in one spot, place a litter box there. Ferrets rarely un-learn a preferred corner.

turtle-basking-time-calculator.name: Turtle Basking Time Calculator
turtle-basking-time-calculator.description: Species-specific basking photoperiod, UV Index target, water and basking-surface temperatures for sliders, painted turtles, musk turtles, tortoises and more.

ui.noteRedEaredSlider: Fully aquatic — needs a large dry dock reachable in one motion.
ui.notePaintedTurtle: Cooler water tolerated; still needs strong UVB.
ui.noteMuskTurtle: Rarely basks — provide a low platform they'll actually use.
ui.noteMapTurtle: Skittish — bask most when tank is in a low-traffic area.
ui.noteRussianTortoise: Land tortoise — soak weekly in shallow warm water.
ui.noteSulcata: Outdoor sunshine is best when weather allows.
ui.neverBaskNote: A turtle that never basks is nearly always cold, sick or scared. Verify the dock is dry, easy to climb, and under real UVB — not filtered through glass or plastic.

goat-hoof-trim-reminder.name: Goat Hoof Trim Reminder
goat-hoof-trim-reminder.description: Track every goat in your herd, set individual trim intervals, and get overdue alerts to prevent hoof rot, laminitis and lameness across dairy, meat and pet goats.

ui.intervalHint: Most goats: 6-8 weeks. Rocky terrain wears hooves and extends interval; damp bedding shortens it.
ui.emptyState: Add goats to see next trim dates.
ui.trimTip: Trim in bright natural light. Cut only the soft, curled outer wall until the sole is flat and level with the toe.

horse-farrier-schedule.name: Horse Farrier Schedule
horse-farrier-schedule.description: Manage barefoot and shod horses on a rolling farrier schedule with configurable intervals and clear overdue warnings so no horse slips past 8 weeks.

ui.intervalHint: Shod horses: typically 6 weeks. Barefoot: 6-8. Faster-growing hooves (spring/summer) shorten cycle.
ui.emptyState: Add horses to build the schedule.
ui.cycleTip: A stretched cycle causes long-toe / low-heel imbalance, which drives navicular pain and hoof cracks. Book the next appointment before the farrier leaves.

vivarium-humidity-calculator.name: Vivarium Humidity Calculator
vivarium-humidity-calculator.description: Compare your enclosure humidity to species-correct ranges for reptiles, amphibians and tortoises — with misting frequency, substrate choice and troubleshooting tips.

ui.noteBeardedDragon: Excess humidity causes respiratory infection. Aim under 40%.
ui.substrateLeopardGecko: Tile or paper towel; humid hide with moss for shedding
ui.noteLeopardGecko: Dedicated humid hide with damp sphagnum moss is essential for shedding.
ui.mistingCrestedGecko: Heavy mist 1× at night, light 1× morning
ui.noteCrestedGecko: Allow humidity to drop to 50% between mistings — constant wet causes bacterial skin infection.
ui.noteBallPython: Boost to 70% only during shed cycle.
ui.noteCornSnake: Humid hide during shed prevents dysecdysis.
ui.mistingChameleon: 2-3× daily heavy mist + dripper/fogger at night
ui.noteChameleon: Chameleons drink only from moving droplets — a dripper is required, not a bowl.
ui.noteDayGecko: Live plants stabilise humidity better than any mister.
ui.noteRussianTortoise: Arid species — high humidity causes shell rot.
ui.substrateRedEaredSlider: None in water, none on dock
ui.noteRedEaredSlider: Ambient humidity from the water is usually sufficient.
ui.pillDry: Too dry — add misting / bigger water bowl / cover part of screen top
ui.pillWet: Too wet — increase ventilation, reduce misting, swap to more absorbent substrate
ui.hygrometerNote: Measure with a digital hygrometer at animal height. Analog dial hygrometers are typically off by 10-15%.

pet-breed-identifier.description: Upload a photo of your dog, cat or small pet and get an AI-powered breed identification with likely mixes, visible traits, temperament and care snapshot.

pet-body-condition-photo.name: Pet Body Condition Score from Photo
pet-body-condition-photo.description: Upload a top-down or side-profile photo and get an educational Body Condition Score on the veterinary 1–9 scale, plus an action plan.

ui.headerTitle: Veterinary Pet Body Condition & Morphometric Analyzer
ui.headerDesc: Analyze top-down and side photos alongside palpation markers to determine your pet's exact WSAVA Body Condition Score, ideal weight target, and daily calorie plan.
ui.presetHealthyNotes: Labrador mix with clearly felt ribs, clean hourglass waist, and fit abdominal tuck.
ui.presetBeagleNotes: Ribs difficult to palpate, flat straight back with no waist, slight belly bulge.
ui.presetCatNotes: Domestic Shorthair with rounded flanks and fat pad, ribs require firm pressure.
ui.presetRescueNotes: Rescue dog with prominent ribs, visible hip pins, and extreme tucked groin.
ui.goalLoss: Target gradual loss of 1.0–1.5% body weight per week
ui.goalGain: Controlled weight gain with calorie-dense balanced diet
ui.goalBalance: Caloric balance for active vitality and lean muscle
ui.card1Desc: Accurate weight and species allow precise Resting Energy Requirement (RER) calculations.
ui.pouchDesc: Loose belly flap is normal feline anatomy, not visceral fat.
ui.card2Desc: Veterinary visual scoring requires observing both the dorsal hourglass waist and the lateral abdominal tuck.
ui.angleAHint: Stand above pet, looking down at spine & waist
ui.card3Desc: Tactile palpation is the gold standard in veterinary medicine to distinguish lean muscle from subcutaneous fat.
ui.ribHelp1: Sharp, prominent ribs with zero fat padding. Feels like sharp knuckles of a clenched fist (BCS 1–2).
ui.ribHelp2: Ribs easily felt with no pressure; clearly visible on short-haired breeds (BCS 3–4).
ui.ribHelp3: IDEAL: Ribs easily felt with light hand sweep—feels like knuckles on the back of a flat hand (BCS 5).
ui.ribHelp4: Ribs felt only with firm finger pressure under a noticeable fat blanket (BCS 6–7).
ui.ribHelp5: Ribs cannot be palpated under thick, dense adipose tissue. Feels like the palm of your hand (BCS 8–9).
ui.waistHelp1: Severe, drastic waist indentation with sunken hollow flanks behind ribcage (BCS 1–2).
ui.waistHelp2: Marked, narrow waistline clearly visible with prominent pelvic pins (BCS 3–4).
ui.waistHelp3: IDEAL: Smooth, well-proportioned hourglass waist tapering cleanly behind ribs (BCS 5).
ui.waistHelp4: Straight rectangular flank line; waistline is flat, absent, or barely discernible (BCS 6–7).
ui.waistHelp5: Distended, barrel-shaped or pear-shaped bulge outward from the ribcage (BCS 8–9).
ui.tuckHelp1: Dramatic, steep upward abdominal tuck carving deeply into groin (BCS 1–3).
ui.tuckHelp2: IDEAL: Clean, clear upward abdominal slope from posterior ribcage into groin (BCS 4–5).
ui.tuckHelp3: Flat underline parallel to floor; abdominal tuck is absent or muted (BCS 6–7).
ui.tuckHelp4: Pendulous, rounded belly hanging downward with fat pad swaying during motion (BCS 8–9).
ui.timelineLabel: Safe projected timeline to ideal BCS:
ui.knuckleLi1Rest: : Run your fingers across your flat knuckles. You can feel bones easily without pressure.
ui.knuckleLi2Rest: : Run your fingers over the sharp raised knuckles of a tight fist.
ui.knuckleLi3Rest: : Feel the fleshy pad below your thumb. If your pet's ribs feel like this, they have excessive adipose padding.
ui.reportBadgeAi: Generated via Multi-Angle Vision AI Model
ui.reportBadgeClinical: Generated via WSAVA Clinical Morphometrics Protocol
ui.reportValidated: Validated against WSAVA Nutritional Assessment Guidelines & APOP standards.
ui.matrixDesc: Reference criteria used by veterinary practices worldwide to assess adiposity in companion canines and felines.
ui.matrixUnderRibsText: Highly prominent, visible from distance; zero palpable fat layer.
ui.matrixUnderWaistText: Extreme hourglass indentation with hollow sunken flanks.
ui.matrixUnderRiskText: Muscle loss, hypothermia vulnerability, immune suppression.
ui.matrixIdealRibsText: Easily palpable with light hand sweep; feels like flat knuckles.
ui.matrixIdealWaistText: Proportional hourglass waist visible behind ribs; clear abdominal tuck.
ui.matrixIdealStandardText: Proven +1.8 to 2.5 years longer lifespan and lower osteoarthritis rate.
ui.matrixOverRibsText: Palpable only with deep pressure or completely obscured under thick fat.
ui.matrixOverWaistText: Absent or bulging outward like a barrel; pendulous sagging belly fat.
ui.matrixOverRiskText: 4x feline diabetes risk, cruciate tears, cardiac strain, chronic inflammation.
ui.fallbackTimeline: - **Estimated Timeline to Ideal BCS:** **~{{weeks}} weeks** at a safe 1.0–1.5% weekly reduction rate.
ui.fallbackFooter: *This evaluation combines standardized WSAVA morphometrics, user palpation sweep diagnostics, and veterinary energy expenditure equations.*
ui.reportClipboardTitle: FURTOOLS VETERINARY BODY CONDITION SCORE (BCS) REPORT
ui.reportClipboardFooter: Generated via FurTools Pet Body Condition Photo Analyzer (https://www.furtools.com/tools/pet-body-condition-photo)
ui.tier1RibFeel: Ribs, lumbar vertebrae, and pelvic bones are razor-sharp and visible from a distance with zero palpable fat.
ui.tier1Waist: Extreme, severe hourglass waist indentation with sunken hollow flanks.
ui.tier1Tuck: Dramatic, steep abdominal tuck curving sharply up behind ribs.
ui.tier1Fat: Zero fat padding; obvious loss of muscle mass and bony prominences everywhere.
ui.tier1Risk: Severe medical emergency: muscle wasting, immunocompromise, hypothermia risk, organ failure.
ui.tier2RibFeel: Ribs and spine easily visible with minimal palpation needed; zero fat blanket.
ui.tier2Waist: Marked, deep hourglass waist visible from above with prominent hip bones.
ui.tier2Tuck: Prominent abdominal tuck with severe upward slope.
ui.tier2Fat: Tiny trace fat cushion over lumbar vertebrae, minor muscle atrophy.
ui.tier2Risk: High risk of lethargy, reproductive arrest, hypoglycemia, impaired recovery from illness.
ui.tier3RibFeel: Ribs easily felt with no fat cover; tops of vertebrae visible.
ui.tier3Waist: Obvious hourglass waist readily observed when viewed from above.
ui.tier3Tuck: Pronounced abdominal tuck evident upon standing side view.
ui.tier3Fat: Minimal subcutaneous fat, slight fat padding over spine.
ui.tier3Risk: Moderate nutritional deficit; vulnerable to cold weather, low stamina, poor coat quality.
ui.tier4RibFeel: Ribs easily palpable with minimal fat covering; bones distinct but not sharp.
ui.tier4Waist: Clear, proportional hourglass waist clearly visible behind ribs.
ui.tier4Tuck: Crisp, athletic abdominal tuck visible from the side.
ui.tier4Fat: Thin layer of healthy fat; athletic muscling throughout body.
ui.tier4Risk: Excellent metabolic health; associated with peak agility and joint preservation.
ui.tier5RibFeel: Ribs easily palpated with slight hand sweep—feels like knuckles on the back of a flat hand.
ui.tier5Waist: Harmonious hourglass waistline visible from above without sunken hollows.
ui.tier5Tuck: Smooth upward abdominal tuck sloping from ribcage toward groin.
ui.tier5Fat: Balanced, healthy protective fat blanket without excess lumbar or tailhead deposits.
ui.tier5Risk: Peak longevity standard: pets maintained at BCS 5 live an average of 1.8 to 2.5 years longer.
ui.tier6RibFeel: Ribs palpable with slight pressure; covered by a discernible layer of excess fat.
ui.tier6Waist: Waistline discernible from above but flattened and not prominent.
ui.tier6Tuck: Abdominal tuck is slight or blunt when viewed from the side profile.
ui.tier6Fat: Moderate fat layer over lumbar spine and base of tail.
ui.tier6Risk: Early joint wear, low stamina, slight systemic low-grade inflammation.
ui.tier7RibFeel: Ribs difficult to palpate; requires firm thumb and finger pressure.
ui.tier7Waist: Waistline barely discernible or absent; back appears broad and flat.
ui.tier7Tuck: Abdominal tuck is absent; belly underline is flat or parallel to floor.
ui.tier7Fat: Heavy fat deposits over lumbar area and tailbase; neck fat rolls present.
ui.tier7Risk: 2x risk of osteoarthritis, impaired heat tolerance, shortened lifespan by 1.5+ years.
ui.tier8RibFeel: Ribs palpable only with deep, heavy finger pressure or cannot be felt at all.
ui.tier8Waist: Zero waistline; back is distinctly widened and flanks bulge outward like a barrel.
ui.tier8Tuck: Abdominal tuck completely absent; belly hangs low with pendulous fat pads.
ui.tier8Fat: Massive fat padding over lumbar spine, neck, tailhead, and thorax.
ui.tier8Risk: Severe danger: 4x risk of diabetes (cats), CCL ligament rupture, respiratory compromise.
ui.tier9RibFeel: Ribs completely impossible to feel under thick, dense blanket of adipose tissue.
ui.tier9Waist: Back is convex/barrel-shaped; flanks distended outward with prominent fat pads.
ui.tier9Tuck: Pendulous, swinging belly with zero tuck; fat rolls sway during movement.
ui.tier9Fat: Massive fat masses along spine, neck, limbs, tailhead, and inguinal area.
ui.tier9Risk: Critical medical condition: extreme systemic inflammation, cardiac overload, mobility loss.

dog-wolf-coyote-identifier.description: Upload a photo of a canid and find out whether it is a domestic dog, wolf, coyote, fox or hybrid — with the field marks that drove the answer.
