tarantula-enclosure-size-calculator.name: Tarantula Enclosure Size Calculator
tarantula-enclosure-size-calculator.description: Work out the safe floor space, height and substrate depth for your tarantula based on diagonal leg span and whether it is terrestrial, arboreal or fossorial.

ui.noteSling: Slings do best in small vials or 2-4 oz deli cups — oversized homes make feeding response poor.
ui.noteRehouse: Rehouse only when the spider has hardened after a moult (7-10 days).
ui.noteTerrestrial: Height above 1.5× leg span risks a fatal abdominal rupture from falls.
ui.noteArboreal: Provide cork bark slabs and fake foliage as vertical anchors.
ui.noteWater: Always include a shallow water dish, regardless of species.

tarantula-feeding-schedule.name: Tarantula Feeding Schedule
tarantula-feeding-schedule.description: Get a feeding interval, prey size limit and monthly feeding count for your tarantula, with automatic pre-moult adjustments.

ui.preySling: Pre-killed cricket leg or flightless fruit fly
ui.premoultLabel: Showing pre-moult signs (dark abdomen, refusing food, webbing up)
ui.noteRemove: Remove uneaten prey within 24 hours — crickets can injure a moulting spider.
ui.noteResume: Resume feeding 7-10 days after the moult, once fangs darken.
ui.notePlump: A plump, rounded abdomen means you can safely extend the interval.
ui.noteWater: Fresh water must always be available; tarantulas dehydrate faster than they starve.

hedgehog-wheel-size-calculator.name: Hedgehog Wheel Size Calculator
hedgehog-wheel-size-calculator.description: Calculate the minimum safe wheel diameter for your African pygmy hedgehog and check whether your current running surface is safe.

ui.statMinHint: Back must stay flat while running
ui.noteSpine: A wheel that curves the spine upward is too small — the back should look level from the side.
ui.noteWire: Wire or barred wheels trap toes and cause degloving injuries. Only solid surfaces are safe.
ui.noteClean: Clean the wheel nightly; hedgehogs almost always defecate while running.

hedgehog-diet-calculator.name: Hedgehog Diet Calculator
hedgehog-diet-calculator.description: Estimate daily calories and food portions for an African pygmy hedgehog based on weight, activity level and whether you want it to gain, hold or lose weight.

ui.noteKibble: Choose a kibble with 30-35% protein, under 15% fat and a named animal protein first.
ui.noteNever: Never feed milk, grapes, raisins, avocado, onion, chocolate or raw egg.
ui.noteWeigh: Weigh weekly on a kitchen scale — a 10% change in either direction warrants a vet check.

axolotl-tank-temperature-calculator.name: Axolotl Tank Temperature Checker
axolotl-tank-temperature-calculator.description: Check axolotl water temperature against safe ranges in Celsius or Fahrenheit and get practical cooling fixes when it runs too warm.

ui.verdictTooCold: Too cold — metabolism and digestion stall
ui.verdictCool: Cool but survivable — feeding response drops
ui.verdictWarm: Warm — stress risk, watch for curled gills
ui.verdictDangerous: Dangerous — heat stress, fungal infection and death risk
ui.noteHeater: Never use an aquarium heater. Axolotls are cold-water amphibians.
ui.noteCool: Cool with clip-on fans across the surface (2-3 °C drop), frozen water bottles, or an aquarium chiller for a permanent fix.
ui.noteShade: Keep the tank out of direct sunlight and away from heating vents.
ui.noteSigns: Curled forward gills, floating and refusing food are classic heat-stress signs.

axolotl-tank-size-calculator.name: Axolotl Tank Size Calculator
axolotl-tank-size-calculator.description: Calculate the minimum tank volume, floor footprint and hide count for one or more axolotls, plus flow advice for your filter type.

ui.flowCanister: Use a spray bar aimed at the glass
ui.flowHob: Baffle the outflow with filter floss
ui.footprintHint: Floor space matters more than height
ui.noteFloor: Floor area beats water column — axolotls are benthic and rarely use vertical space.
ui.noteSand: Use fine sand or bare bottom. Gravel causes fatal impaction.
ui.noteMulti: House only same-size axolotls; larger ones will bite gills and limbs off smaller tank mates.
ui.noteSolitary: Axolotls are solitary and thrive alone.

sugar-glider-diet-calculator.name: Sugar Glider Diet Calculator
sugar-glider-diet-calculator.description: Calculate nightly food weight for your sugar glider colony and split it correctly between staple mix, produce and protein.

ui.noteDusk: Serve at dusk and remove leftovers each morning — wet diets spoil quickly.
ui.noteCalcium: Maintain a roughly 2:1 calcium-to-phosphorus ratio; imbalance causes hind-leg paralysis (HLP).
ui.noteNever: Never feed chocolate, onion, garlic, avocado, raw nuts in bulk or anything sugar-free (xylitol).
ui.noteColony: Sugar gliders are colony animals — keeping one alone causes serious stress behaviours.

sugar-glider-cage-size-calculator.name: Sugar Glider Cage Size Calculator
sugar-glider-cage-size-calculator.description: Get minimum cage width, depth and height for your sugar glider colony, plus a bar-spacing safety check and pouch count.

ui.maxBarHint: ½ inch or less, horizontal bars preferred
ui.noteHeight: Height matters most — gliders leap and glide vertically.
ui.noteWire: Use PVC-coated or stainless wire; galvanised zinc can cause metal toxicity.
ui.noteFill: Fill with branches, fleece ropes, a wodent wheel (11-12" solid) and rotating foraging toys.

chinchilla-dust-bath-schedule.name: Chinchilla Dust Bath Schedule
chinchilla-dust-bath-schedule.description: Build a chinchilla dust-bath schedule based on room humidity and coat condition, with session length and a next-bath reminder.

ui.noteLeaving: Leaving dust in the cage 24/7 causes eye irritation and over-drying.
ui.noteDehumidifier: Run a dehumidifier — chinchillas need under 50% humidity and below 24 °C to avoid heat stroke and fungus.
ui.noteTemp: Keep the room under 24 °C; chinchillas overheat easily.
ui.noteReuse: Reuse dust 2-3 times, sifting droppings out, then replace it.

chinchilla-cage-size-calculator.name: Chinchilla Cage Size Calculator
chinchilla-cage-size-calculator.description: Calculate minimum chinchilla cage dimensions, total usable floor area, level count and bar spacing safety for one or more chinchillas.

ui.floorHint: Target {{sqft}} sq ft of total shelf + floor space
ui.noteShelves: Use kiln-dried pine or fleece-covered shelves — wire flooring causes bumblefoot.
ui.noteTemp: Keep the cage away from windows and vents; 15-21 °C is the safe temperature band.
ui.noteInclude: Include a hay rack, chew blocks, a hide per chinchilla and a 15" solid saucer or wheel.

tortoise-hibernation-planner.name: Tortoise Hibernation Planner
tortoise-hibernation-planner.description: Plan a safe tortoise hibernation with species-specific duration, a Jackson ratio body-condition check, target temperatures and a full date timeline.

ui.noteHermann: Classic Mediterranean hibernator — 4-8 °C fridge method works well.
ui.noteRussian: Tolerates cooler brumation; ensure a full pre-hibernation health check.
ui.noteGreek: Shorter periods suit captive Greeks; libyan/tunisian races should not hibernate.
ui.noteSulcata: African species — NEVER hibernate. Keep warm year-round.
ui.noteBoxTurtle: North American box turtles brumate; use a controlled cool box or fridge.
ui.weightLossHint: Max 1% of body weight per month
ui.fastStartHint: (gut must be empty — 2-4 weeks depending on size)
ui.noteVet: A pre-hibernation vet check (weight, eyes, mouth, worm count) is essential every year.
ui.noteWeigh: Weigh weekly during hibernation. Losing more than 1% of body weight per month means wake the tortoise immediately.
ui.noteNever: Never hibernate a sick, underweight, or first-year hatchling tortoise without veterinary approval.

quail-coop-size-calculator.name: Quail Coop Size Calculator
quail-coop-size-calculator.description: Calculate quail coop floor space, safe ceiling height, feeder and waterer counts and the correct male-to-hen ratio for coturnix, bobwhite or button quail.

ui.ceilingHint: Low, padded — quail 'boink' straight up when startled
ui.noteMales: Keep no more than 1 male per 4-5 hens (about {{males}} male{{plural}} for this flock) to prevent hen injuries.
ui.noteWire: Use ½ inch hardware cloth — chicken wire will not stop rats, snakes or weasels.
ui.noteCover: Provide overhead cover and hides; quail panic in open, brightly lit spaces.
ui.noteCage: Sloped wire floors ease egg collection but add a solid resting mat to prevent foot sores.
ui.noteLitter: Deep litter of pine shavings or sand, turned weekly, keeps ammonia down.

dietNote.finch: Grass seeds, sprouted seed mix, egg food during molting, and finely chopped dark greens.
dietNote.budgie: Prone to fatty liver and iodine deficiency; convert to high-potency micro-pellets with fresh leafy greens.
dietNote.lovebird: Active foragers; feed chopped broccoli florets, carrots, sprouted lentils, and low-fat pellets.
dietNote.cockatiel: Seed addiction causes renal and hepatic disease; transition slowly to 60% pellets and fresh orange/green vegetables.
dietNote.conure: Loves textured whole foods; steam squash, sweet potato cubes, bell peppers, and chili peppers.
dietNote.african-grey: Extreme vulnerability to hypocalcemia; requires bioavailable calcium (kale, collards) and raw red palm fruit oil.
dietNote.amazon: Extremely prone to obesity and atherosclerosis; strictly cap seeds and fatty nuts under 3%.
dietNote.eclectus: UNIQUE DIGESTION: Long digestive tract. Synthetic fortified pellets cause toe-tapping/wing-flipping! Diet must be 75%+ fresh raw produce & sprouts.
dietNote.cockatoo: High risk of lipomas (fat tumors); emphasize cruciferous vegetables and foraging toys.
dietNote.macaw: Naturally high-fat requirement; needs 2â3 raw, human-grade in-shell walnuts, Brazil nuts, or macadamia nuts daily.

none.title: Full Flighted (Veterinary Recommended)
lines: Cardiovascular Health: Flying uses 10–20× more energy than walking, preventing fatal avian atherosclerosis and fatty liver.
Psychological Confidence: Flighted birds exhibit significantly lower rates of chronic scream-calling, phobias, and feather self-mutilation.
Home Safety Mandate: All ceiling fans MUST be turned OFF, windows covered with decals or blinds, open cookware covered, and doors closed.

conservative.title: Conservative Micro-Clip (Glide Preserved)
lines: Trim only the outer 4 to 6 primary flight feathers on BOTH wings symmetrically.
Allows the bird to glide safely to the floor at a 45° angle; prevents upward lift while eliminating crash landing fractures.
NEVER trim secondary flight feathers (inner wing) or covert protective feathers.

aggressive.title: Severe / Single-Wing Clip (Strictly Prohibited)
lines: Severe Danger: Cutting too short causes the bird to drop like a rock, shattering the keel bone (sternum) and splitting the skin.
Single-Wing Asymmetry: Clipping one wing causes catastrophic corkscrew spins into walls and floors.
Blood Feather Lethality: Trimming dark, active growing blood feathers causes profuse hemorrhaging.

hayNote.timothy2: 2nd Cut Timothy: Gold standard balance of rough fiber (32%), moderate protein, and soft green leaves.
hayNote.timothy1: 1st Cut Timothy: Coarser, ultra-high fiber; optimal for wearing down rapid-growing dental molars.
hayNote.orchard: Orchard Grass: Softer and sweeter; ideal for allergy-sensitive owners and picky rabbits.
hayNote.meadow: Meadow Grass: Diverse floral blend; stimulates natural foraging behavior.
hayNote.alfalfa: Alfalfa Hay: High calcium/protein legume hay; for young bunnies (<6 months) or nursing does ONLY.

ui.sleepCageBody: A smaller dedicated sleep cage in a quiet, dark spare bedroom prevents sleep disruption from family TV/kitchen activity and eliminates night frights.

budgie.name: Budgerigar (Australian Grassland)
budgie.hormonal: If female budgies start searching for dark nesting corners, extend sleep to 12 hours of total darkness to suppress breeding hormones.

canary.name: Canary / Finch
canary.hormonal: Natural daylight changes stimulate spring singing; keep photoperiod consistent to avoid out-of-season molting.

cockatiel.name: Cockatiel
cockatiel.hormonal: CRITICAL FOR FEMALE COCKATIELS: Chronic egg laying is triggered by long daylight (>14 hrs). Maintain 12–14 hours of total dark coverage to prevent fatal egg binding.

lovebird.name: Lovebird
lovebird.hormonal: Cover cage with breathable blackout fabric; prevent access to shredded paper or enclosed dark huts.

conure.name: Conure (Green Cheek / Sun)
conure.hormonal: Sleep deprivation triggers aggressive screaming and territorial cage aggression. Provide quiet sleep retreat.

african-grey.name: African Grey
african-grey.suggestion: 8:00 PM – 8:00 AM (12 hours in dedicated sleep cage)
african-grey.hormonal: African Greys are highly prone to psychogenic night frights and feather plucking if disturbed by evening TV light.

amazon.name: Amazon Parrot
amazon.hormonal: Spring hormonal 'hot-headed' behavior is reduced by enforcing 12+ hours of strict uninterrupted darkness.

cockatoo.name: Cockatoo
cockatoo.hormonal: Inadequate sleep leads directly to severe neurotic screaming and self-mutilation (feather chewing/picking).

macaw.name: Large Macaw
macaw.hormonal: Equatorial jungle species naturally evolved with equal 12-hour day / 12-hour night cycles.

ui.bannerBody: This fluid therapy calculator adheres to the **AAHA (American Animal Hospital Association)** and **WSAVA** fluid therapy guidelines for canine post-operative recovery, shock resuscitation, and dehydration restoration. Always monitor patient lung sounds, PCV/TP, and urine output to prevent fluid overload.
ui.tierMarkers0: Moist, pink gums; immediate skin turgor recoil (<1s); bright alert eyes; capillary refill time (CRT) < 2s.
ui.tierMarkers5: Slightly tacky mucous membranes; normal skin turgor; eyes normal; CRT ~2s.
ui.tierMarkers7: Dry/sticky gums; slight loss of skin turgor (delayed skin fold recoil 2–3s); CRT 2–3s; mild depression.
ui.tierMarkers10: Marked skin tenting (skin stays pinched >3s); dull sunken eyes (enophthalmos); dry pale gums; CRT > 3s; cold paws.
ui.tierMarkers12: Persistent skin tenting; deeply sunken eyes; signs of hypovolemic shock; weak rapid pulse; cold extremities; depressed consciousness.
ui.correctionHint: Deficit volume is distributed across this duration.
ui.lossesHint: Compensates for surgical fluids, drains, and gastrointestinal loss.
ui.dripOpt15: Standard Macro-drip Set (15 gtt/mL) — Common for medium/large dogs
ui.dripOpt10: Heavy Macro-drip Set (10 gtt/mL) — Large & Giant breeds
ui.dripOpt60: Pediatric Micro-drip Set (60 gtt/mL) — Small dogs & puppies (<10 kg)
ui.pumpRateHint: Continuous IV infusion rate during recovery
ui.urineAfter: (1.0 to 2.0 mL/kg/hr) to confirm renal recovery and prevent anuria.
ui.emptyState: Enter your dog's weight to calculate the fluid prescription.
ui.refTitle: Post-Operative Fluid Monitoring & Fluid Overload Warning Signs
ui.refCrystalloidsBody: Balanced electrolyte solutions such as **Lactated Ringer's Solution (LRS)**, **Normosol-R**, or **Plasmalyte-A** are preferred. Avoid pure 0.9% NaCl for prolonged maintenance unless hypochloremia or Addisonian crisis is present.
ui.refOverloadBody: Serous nasal discharge, chemosis (swelling of the conjunctiva), tachypnea (rapid breathing), moist lung crackles, restlessness, and sudden excessive body weight gain. Reduce rate immediately if noted.
ui.refHypothermiaBody: Use fluid warmers or warm IV lines when administering fluids post-surgery to prevent anesthesia-induced hypothermia, which delays drug clearance and prolongs recovery times.
